units: <cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 4:2">Ber. IV, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="A03216"><he>אָרַע</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:1:5">Y. Ab. Zar. II, 40ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>שלא תמציא לו ת׳</he> that thou provide no snare for him (temptation to sodomy).

<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:4">Snh. VII, 4</cite> <he>לפי שבאת לאדם ת׳ על ידה … דבר אחר וכ׳</he> because an offence has come to a man through it (the animal with which sodomy has been committed), therefore the text says, that it must be stoned; another reason, (it must be put to death,) lest the animal pass by in the street, and men say, this is the animal for which such and such a man was stoned to death.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 55a:12">Ib. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>ת׳ וקלון וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="S01269"><he>קָלוֹן</he> I</cite>. Mekh. B’shall. s. 1, end <he>המקנה … הם היו ת׳ וכ׳</he> the animals which the God-fearing (among the Egyptians) had saved became a snare (cause of evil) to Israel.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 57b:5">Kidd. 57ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 14:7">Lev. XIV, 7</cite>) <he>לא אמרה תורה שלח לת׳</he> the Law would not order the bird to be sent off for a possible offence (which would be the case, if the bird sent off were not permitted to be used); <cite ref="Chullin 115a">Ḥull. 115ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 140a">140ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 67b">Yoma 67ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 3:2:5">Y. Dem. III, 23ᶜ</cite> top <he>עושה ת׳ באים וכ׳</he> he prepares a snare (possibility of sin) to those coming after him.
<cite ref="Yoma 86b:18">Yoma 86ᵇ</cite> <he>שלות … ת׳</he> the prosperity of the wicked ends in a snare (leads them to sin).
<cite ref="Chullin 53b:6">Ḥull. 53ᵇ</cite>, a. e. (in Chald. dict.) <he>אתי בהו לידי ת׳</he> one may be led to commit an offence through them; a. fr.
